# Copilot Instructions — shizuoka-demo-cesium-BD

Customer-ready CesiumJS Sandcastle demo suite for Shizuoka Prefecture (Virtual
Shizuoka LiDAR / PLATEAU buildings / bathymetry), built for a PSS partner demo.

## Architecture

- **Source of truth:** hand-edited demos live in `sandcastle/*.js`:
  - `disaster-response-hydrodynamic.js` — Demo 1, Abe River flood response
  - `point-cloud-vs-buildings.js` — Demo 2, LiDAR vs PLATEAU buildings
  - `voxel-water-saturation.js` — Demo 3, voxel analytics
  - `timeseries-pointcloud-change.js` — Demo 4, time-series point cloud change
- **Compiled output (do not hand-edit):** `shizuoka-sandcastles.html` (root
  landing page) and `docs/index.html` (GitHub Pages copy, served at
  `https://jastman.github.io/shizuoka-demo-cesium-BD/`). Both are generated by
  `build.js`, which deflate/base64-encodes each `sandcastle/*.js` file into an
  embedded Sandcastle share URL and stamps a `BUILD_UTC` timestamp.

## Critical workflow: always rebuild after editing a demo

**Editing a `sandcastle/*.js` file has NO effect on the live demo until you run
`node build.js`.** Several past sessions burned many turns "debugging" errors
(e.g. a stale Ion asset 404) that were actually just an unbuilt HTML file
still serving an old compiled payload. After *any* change to
`sandcastle/*.js`:

1. Run `node build.js` (regenerates both `shizuoka-sandcastles.html` and
   `docs/index.html`, updates `BUILD_UTC`).
2. Confirm the change is reflected in the generated HTML (e.g. grep for the
   asset ID / string you changed) before telling the user it's fixed.
3. Commit the source `.js` files together with both generated HTML files in
   the same commit — never commit source without the rebuilt output, or the
   two will drift out of sync.

## Multiple worktrees — verify you're in the right one

This repo is frequently worked in many parallel git worktrees (one per
branch/feature). This has caused repeated confusion: agents editing/verifying
files in the wrong worktree, or a user pasting an error from one worktree's
`shizuoka-sandcastles.html` while the agent works in a different one.

- Before debugging a reported error, confirm which worktree/branch the
  user's file path or Sandcastle link actually points to — check the full
  `file:///...` path or branch name given, don't assume it's the current
  session's directory.
- If the code state you see doesn't match what the user describes, say so
  explicitly and ask for the exact file/branch/worktree rather than guessing.
- When asked to publish/update "the" public demo, remember GitHub Pages only
  serves `docs/index.html` from the deployed branch (typically `main`) — a
  fix committed on a feature-branch worktree does not appear live until it's
  merged/pushed to the branch Pages is built from.

## Don't stall silently during verification loops

If a live-verification tool (e.g. Chrome DevTools MCP, Playwright) is
blocked (profile lock, busy browser, etc.), don't just stop — state the
blocker explicitly and either try an alternative verification method
immediately or ask a specific question. Multiple sessions show the user
having to prompt "keep going, why'd you stop" after the agent went quiet
mid-fix.

## Verify live before declaring something fixed

Don't tell the user "this should be fixed, reload the page" without having
actually loaded/inspected the rebuilt output yourself when a browser/preview
tool is available. Several fixes were reported as done and turned out to
still be broken (stale asset ID, wrong worktree, not rebuilt) because the fix
was reasoned about but never visually confirmed.

## Ion asset IDs

Ion asset IDs (terrain, imagery, 3D Tiles) referenced in `sandcastle/*.js`
occasionally become stale (deleted/replaced in the Ion account), causing
opaque 404s like `Resource Not Found: /v1/assets/<id>/endpoint`. When you hit
one:
- Don't assume it's a code bug first — check whether the ID is simply no
  longer valid, and confirm the currently-valid replacement ID with the user
  or repo history before swapping it in.
- Note current known-good IDs in your fix commit message/summary so future
  sessions don't have to rediscover them.
